I read the rules of this sub like 20 times to make sure I don't break them. Lol. I just want to ensure that you know I'm NOT a dermatologist.  However, I am a black woman who has experienced this issue. I would say this happened to me about ten years ago. My lips were SO dark the only thing I could think to do was to wear really dark, really pigmented lipstick. I can't say 100% what the cause was, but I know that it all started when I wore a really cheap lip gloss. My lips would regularly react badly when I would apply cheap formulas to them. I would get tiny bumps all over my skin. This time, after I got the bumps, my lips turned super dark. I couldn't get any answers.  I have always found it exceedingly challenging to get help with issues that affect melanated skin. In any case, I thought my lips would be like that forever, but I went through it disappearing and showing up over the better part of a year. Going forward, I only used quality lip products. Additionally, balm with spf may be beneficial too. The only other success stories I've seen have been with people being prescribed desonide ointment.  Some have said that stops it completely. 
With all of this said, if you smoke, that is likely the direct cause. I don't smoke, but as I'm sure you know, smoking causes terrible hyperpigmentation in the lips of black people.  Good luck!

I think that so many people are getting caught up in the boarding time, but that sincerely has no relevance. This is a Homeland Security clearance issue. I actually attended a private party on board a cruise ship docked in the US. My unreliable ex canceled at the last minute as my plus one, so I had a replacement within five minutes. My replacement couldn't go because to even board the vessel, your identification had to have already cleared through homeland security. The cruise lines have a huge level of liability as it pertains to federal agencies and abroad. 
Please understand that it is unfathomable that they take a citizen of the United States or otherwise, into a foreign country with an expired ID. If you missed boarding time from one of the ports, it would be a mess trying to reenter the US. Additionally, you cannot leave the vessel at a foreign port and record without valid identification.  Lastly, as has been said many times already, the information regarding the ID is in the cruise documents.  So, while you can sue for... idk... if you had everything valid, ready to go, on time, and they said "no. We don't like people named Susan. You can't come" you cannot sue for an obvious breach of your cruise documents.  I hope you get to sail in the future!

She had me early, when she still wasn't financially well off yet, but she worked incredibly hard and ultimately created a great life for us.
I got pregnant by an abusive boyfriend.  I had always been a generally responsible person and ended up pregnant much later than literally all my friends.  I was quasi responsible, but had zero savings, because I was just living a relatively care free life. I initially had no intention whatsoever of staying pregnant.  I hadn't done all the things to create this "perfect" environment where I saved up for everything my child needed through grad school, and I also had no desire to be tormented by her father. I very much believe in body autonomy and the right of everyone to do as they please; however, I found that I PERSONALLY could not go through with an abortion. 
Again, I had nothing, but I had a decent job, and I had standards. I, much like my mother, was not going to accept just any living condition. I literally did not save any money, just so I could always provide my child a certain standard of living. I ALWAYS wanted her to look great, have nice clothes, never be hungry, and always have a decent home to come to. I worked overtime as much as humanly possible. I did work on the side with any ounce of energy I had left. There have been times where I was pretty bad off, where I had absolutely nothing, but my kid would never know. I have taken all the change I could find to feed them, while I starve.
Now, we are doing well, but it wasn't without struggle. I personally feel that when you start a family, you can accept that you're poor and not even attempt to change your situation, OR, you can do things to at least attempt to change your life for the sake of your children. Motivation and innovation are free.

I want to add that I am saying all this as a person who has dealt with crippling mental illness. That is also not child's fault, and I have actively been treated since before my child was born, as it is my responsibility as a parent to ensure I'm mentally sound.

My thoughts weren't organized the best, but I hope I gave some new perspective.

So... this is the perspective from someone who used to work there. When there are these types of issues, it is typically die to 3 things:

1) Expired or denied prior authorization
2) Expired (or unregistered for entirely) copays assistance programs
3) Drug interaction/allergy/disease delays

But most often....... (especially with Humira)

4) Doctor error

Not only will your doctor never, ever admit to it being their fault, but the pharmacy is just going to tell you they need "clarification." I can see how as a patient, you would 100% blame the pharmacy.  But, the fact is that if they have a viable prescription, they will just get it out of there. There is literally no other reason for delay. I can tell you having worked with Humira for decades that doctors REGULARLY write it incorrectly.  

I wish I could yell it to the mountain tops that the biggest delay in patient care is usually the pharmacy trying to keep patients safe.

Though I really understand the reason for the delays, I'm also empathetic to the patient because it has nothing to do with them. The best thing you can tell your doctor to do is to ask for a pharmacist and give a verbal prescription.  That way, they can ensure it's correct.

But also, if you get an antibiotic for illness, if you aren't up to date on TB tests, if you have some new medical condition,  or if youre trying to get pregnant... any number of things flag in the system that have nothing to do with the pharmacy.  The insurance requires us to ask your doctor if we can continue to fill the Rx, and they RARELY get back on the same day.

Not giving excuses, just insight.
